newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian Commodities Roundup - Oct 24.

text.p: Copper and aluminium prices rallied briskly on Wednesday propelled by trade and speculative buying after a dull few weeks marked by disappointing seasonal demand.
Some analysts saw a prospect of further gains in the industrial metals sector although copper, at least, met resistance during Wednesday's advance which was also fuelled by short covering.
London Metal Exchange (LME) three-months aluminium succeeded in closing the afternoon above the psychological threshold of $1,400 per tonne.
It ran up to a day's high at $1,411 before closing $39 up from Tuesday at $1,406.
Copper was not quite so buoyant. It raced above key technical resistance at $1,970 per tonne and hit $1,990 in the morning but ended at $1,976.
Producer sales and profit-taking were the reason why prices came off the highs.
Traders say that further falls in LME warehouse stocks are expected in aluminium. Copper inventories have already fallen by more than 100,000 tonnes since the end of August.

Copper has ignored news this week of the arrest on forgery charges of Yasuo Hamanaka, the trader who dominated the copper market until last June when Sumitomo Corp of Japan sacked him and alleged he ran up $2.6 billion of losses on rogue deals.

CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby December dropping late on commercial selling with talk Turkey may turn back shipments of U.S. wheat also mentioned, traders said. Traders said Cargill Inc and Merrill Lynch Futures each sold nearly two million bushels of December near the close. Wheat held firm much of the session on an impressive recovery in soybeans and on a short-term technical bounce. Concerns about the fate of U.S. wheat exports to Turkey apparently stemmed from rumors Turkey may be clamping down on inspections of U.S. wheat cargoes. Wheat closed one cent pwer bushel lower to two cents higher, with December down one at $3.98-1/2 and March down 1/2 at $3.91. Technical indicators in wheat remain bearish.

London gold fixed slightly weaker at $383.50 an ounce in the afternoon compared to $383.95 in the morning. Despite a more bullish mood and a gain of $4 an ounce over the past three days, gold appeared to encounter stiff resistance. New York precious metals futures ended mostly slightly lower Wednesday, after two days of gains earlier this week, but platinum ended higher. COMEX December gold ended down 20 cents at $385.90 an ounce, after trading a narrow $386.30-385.40 range, inside Tuesday's wide range which included a two week high at $386.50. In bullion trade Wednesday, spot gold ended quoted $383.60/384.10.

Crude oil prices stayed firm just above $24 for a barrel of the benchmark Brent Blend from the North Sea but the rally of recent days was not reignited by late Wednesday. The NYMEX oil complex ended lower Wednesday on a sharp decline in heating oil after an inventory report showed a bearish stock build in heat and high production levels for distillate, traders and analysts said. December crude ended the day 67 cents a barrel lower at $24.86.

Dull and rangebound activity persisted in the CSCE world sugar market as thin volume and a dearth of news remained the day's main features. March closed up 0.02 to 10.65, having ranged from 10.68 to 10.59. The back months ended the day 0.05 to 0.01 higher. Volume was estimated at only 6,487 lots.
Support remained at 10.50 in March and resistance at 10.80.
